links_touching_record.rationale: The qualification plan's level L2 states its strategy as the unit tests with their recorded oracle basis, and pass criteria PC-002, PC-003, PC-004 and PC-005 are all stated against what the unit test specification measured. The plan cannot be assessed without knowing what the unit level actually established.

The qualification plan's level L3 is defined as the integration plan, and its pass criterion PC-007 restates the integration levels' exit criteria. Qualification of integrated software presupposes an integration plan that has been executed, which it has not been.

The summary reports the state the qualification plan describes, including the eleven pass criteria of which six are unmet. If the plan is revised, the summary's verdict is no longer accurate and must be reissued.
Deficiencies VDR-004, VDR-007, VDR-008 and VDR-010 are stated against the qualification plan's levels L1 to L5 and its pass criteria PC-006, PC-008, PC-009, PC-010 and PC-011.

The requirement's three acceptance criteria are 50 ms acquisition period, 100% PEC rejection before database write and 25 ms database publish latency. The plan's pass criterion PC-008 states that all three must be demonstrated against a recorded result, and the specification records that the PEC criterion is covered only on a self-consistency oracle and that neither latency criterion has any oracle at all.

The requirement's four acceptance criteria are 5 ms classification latency, 1 mV threshold accuracy, 1E-6 events/hour false positives under 5 mV Gaussian noise and 2 ms fault-request latency. The plan's PC-009 states that the debounce criterion cannot be met because the detailed design records no debounce in the source, and the specification records that the SOA module's routine outcome is unasserted. This is the weakest requirement-to-verification link in the corpus.

The requirement's three acceptance criteria are 5 ms fault-response latency, 100% auxiliary feedback readback and 100% valid state transitions. The specification records that the contactor driver's only test does not build, so none of the three has any result, and the plan's PC-008 requires a measured clock for the latency criterion.

The qualification plan's level L4 and its results_records_absent section both name this record as the blocked qualification execution, execution_kind none with outcome blocked. The plan cannot claim any qualification coverage until this record carries a result, and the record cannot carry a result until the SW Qualification Test Specification the plan says is absent exists.

independence.ai_authorship_disclaimer: An AI-authored review is NOT an independent review, and an AI-authored plan is not an independently checked plan. Independence in the ASPICE sense requires a person who did not author the code. No such person has reviewed any artefact in this corpus. This statement is not a disclaimer attached for form: it is the reason PC-011 is unmet and will remain unmet until a human performs the review.

limitations: This plan is a plan. It demonstrates nothing about the product and its existence changes no verification status by itself.
Of the 5 levels, 1 is partially executed, 1 is executed once on a host at a tree state the tree has since left, and 3 have not been executed at all.
L5 is unspecified rather than merely unexecuted. There is no target board description, no harness and no authority in this corpus.
The scope is three software requirements. This is not a comment on the product's requirements, which are far more numerous; it is a statement about what this corpus contains.

Pass criteria PC-002, PC-005, PC-006, PC-009, PC-010 and PC-011 are stated as bars and are currently unmet. They are written as criteria precisely so that the gap is a matter of record rather than of impression.

integration.description: Defined by FB2-VER-SIP-000001. No specification and no harness.

qualification_on_host.description: Requirement-level acceptance criteria against the host build. Structurally possible, blocked in practice by the absence of any executed qualification measure.

qualification_on_target.description: The product's own hardware. This is the level that would make a qualification claim meaningful.

static.description: Coding-guideline conformance via the uncrustify pre-commit hook and 26 deviation records. Also: reading the module under test to classify the oracle basis of each test, which is what FB2-VER-UTS-000001 does and is the only static method that produced a finding in this corpus: it is how the 5 vacuous green tests and the SOA module's TODO output verification were found.

unit.description: Ceedling 1.1.9-2209dc2 with CMock 2.7.2 and Unity 2.7.2 over 313 targets, compiled by gcc/clang 17.0.0 on arm64-apple-darwin27, against SIL HL_* interface headers. The one method in this corpus that has produced real execution results.

out_of_scope: Target-hardware verification. No run on the product's own board exists in this corpus, so the target-hardware level of this plan has no assets and no results. This is the single largest exclusion and it is stated first because it is the one a reader is most likely to assume was covered.

System-level and HIL fault reaction. The corpus has HIL and system-qualification test measures and execution records, but they are system records, not software qualification results, and this plan does not restate them as software evidence.
The upstream CI unit runs. coverage-plan.json records that the upstream Unity/CMock CI runs were never captured. The one executed sweep is this corpus's own SIL host harness, not upstream's pipeline.

Static analysis and coding-guideline conformance as a qualification gate. The corpus carries 26 deviation records documenting justified departures from coding guidelines, which is conformance work, not a qualification criterion.

Tool qualification for gcc, clang, Ceedling, CMock, Unity, gcov and the debugger. None of these is qualified in this corpus, so every result they produce inherits an unqualified toolchain. This is stated as a limitation of the results, not as an omission of the plan.
The FreeRTOS and FreeRTOS-TCP trees under src/os/freertos/, and the 1445-file vendored dependencies in the graft graph.

pass_criteria.criterion: Every departure from the coding guidelines is recorded as a deviation with a justification, and no unexplained departure exists.
pass_criteria.why_this_is_the_bar: A guideline departure with no recorded reason is indistinguishable from an unreviewed one, and the guideline's value is entirely in the review it forces.

pass_criteria.criterion: Every test file that the recorded run reports as green contains at least one Unity assertion, and no test file declares zero test cases.
pass_criteria.why_this_is_the_bar: A green verdict that cannot fail is not evidence. On the recorded run 5 of 222 green targets assert nothing and 21 of 313 files declare no test case at all, so this criterion is currently not met and is stated as a bar rather than as a description.

pass_criteria.criterion: Every test group has a recorded oracle basis, and no test whose oracle is the code under test is described as verifying that code.
pass_criteria.why_this_is_the_bar: The 39 PEC assertions in the LTC 6813-1 test compare the product's PEC implementation against the product's own constant tables. That is a drift pin and it is valuable, but a consistently wrong PEC passes all 39. The corpus had to be told this explicitly.

pass_criteria.criterion: Every module under test that a software requirement depends on has at least one test that asserts an outcome, not only an argument check.
pass_criteria.why_this_is_the_bar: The SOA module has three NULL-pointer assertions and a TODO where its outcome check should be. It is the module FB2-SW-SWR-000002 is written about, and no behaviour of it is verified.

pass_criteria.criterion: Every test target in the suite builds, or its exclusion is a recorded decision rather than an omission.
pass_criteria.why_this_is_the_bar: 84 of 313 targets did not build in the recorded run. 17 of those are attributed to the product. A target that does not build is not a coverage question, it is an unresolved defect, and it must not sit inside a coverage figure.

pass_criteria.criterion: A statement-coverage and a branch-coverage measurement exist for every module under test.
pass_criteria.why_this_is_the_bar: This criterion is stated because it is NOT met and its absence is the reason the corpus cannot make a percentage claim. 988 assertions executed is not a coverage number. No coverage tool has been run in this corpus.

pass_criteria.criterion: Each integration level's exit criteria are met, and each is observed at the interface the level names rather than through a mock queue.
pass_criteria.why_this_is_the_bar: A diagnosis raised through a CMock expectation queue is verified as an interaction, not as a reaction. The SOA test is the worked example of a suite that would report green and verify nothing.

pass_criteria.criterion: Every acceptance criterion of FB2-SW-SWR-000001, 000002 and 000003 is demonstrated against a recorded result, including all four timing criteria, against a measured clock.
pass_criteria.why_this_is_the_bar: All three requirements are dominated by latency criteria - 50 ms, 25 ms, 5 ms, 1 ms, 2 ms - and none can be demonstrated on a host harness with no wall-clock oracle. This is the criterion that forces the target-hardware level.

pass_criteria.criterion: The debounce behaviour FB2-SW-SWR-000002 specifies exists in the source, or the criterion is formally withdrawn.
pass_criteria.why_this_is_the_bar: FB2-SW-DSN-000005's own declared_gaps records that the SOA module contains no debounce and no reaction path. A requirement that specifies behaviour the source does not contain is not a verification task, it is a contradiction, and no harness can resolve it.

pass_criteria.criterion: A target-hardware run of the integrated software has been performed, its result recorded with input and output hashes, and its verdict stated.
pass_criteria.why_this_is_the_bar: This is the criterion that distinguishes a verified product from a verified host build of the product's sources. It has not been met, and nothing in this corpus substitutes for it.

pass_criteria.criterion: The verification of every level was performed by a person who did not author the code under verification.
pass_criteria.why_this_is_the_bar: ASPICE independence is a process requirement, not a quality nicety. This corpus has met it nowhere: every record here is AI-authored, human_approval_status is pending on all of them, and an AI-authored review is not independence.

record_verbatim.plan_basis: Written from three things that exist: the three software requirements FB2-SW-SWR-000001, 000002 and 000003 with their acceptance criteria; the one recorded software execution, FB2-VER-EXE-000015 in the as_is profile, which is a macOS arm64 host run of the SIL Ceedling harness over 313 targets; and the measured gaps in FB2-VER-UTS-000001 and FB2-VER-SIP-000001. The plan states what would have to be demonstrated at each level. It records no result, because a plan is not a result and this schema has no field in which one could be smuggled in.

record_verbatim.title: Software Qualification Test Plan: what would have to be true, at which level, for foxBMS 2 to be qualified - and what this corpus can and cannot show

verification_levels.blocker: Partially executed. The deviation records exist and are reviewed; this corpus has not itself run the formatter over the tree, so the evidence is that departures were recorded, not that the tree conforms.
verification_levels.level: L1 static review and coding-guideline conformance
verification_levels.purpose: Establish that the code conforms to the standard it claims before any execution evidence is read.
verification_levels.strategy: The project runs uncrustify as a pre-commit hook; the corpus carries 26 deviation records for justified departures. Conformance is demonstrated by review of the deviation records, not by a generated score.

verification_levels.blocker: Executed once, on a host, at a tree state the tree has since left. 84 of 313 targets did not build. 5 of the 222 green targets assert nothing. The oracle for the safety-monitor SOA module records its own output-verification step as TODO. Detailed design exists for 3 of the 24 modules the source inventory names, so for the other 21 there is no design to verify against even where tests pass.
verification_levels.level: L2 unit verification against detailed design
verification_levels.purpose: Establish that each software unit behaves as its detailed design says, with an oracle that could in principle disagree with the code.
verification_levels.strategy: Each unit's tests, with the oracle basis of each test group recorded. The specification of what is covered, on what oracle, and what is not covered is FB2-VER-UTS-000001; the result of the one recorded sweep is FB2-VER-EXE-000015 in the as_is profile.

verification_levels.blocker: No integration test specification exists, so no step has an oracle, and 4 of the 5 integration levels are not executable in this corpus at all: no FreeRTOS host build, no CAN frame observer, no SPI or DMA, no target hardware.
verification_levels.purpose: Establish that units which are correct in isolation produce the intended behaviour when combined, across real interfaces.
verification_levels.strategy: Bottom-up in five levels with entry and exit criteria, ordered by measured coupling. Specified in FB2-VER-SIP-000001.

verification_levels.blocker: FB2-VER-EXE-000008 is execution_kind none with outcome blocked. The five network-security measures state what a passing run would have to observe and what their oracle cannot see, and none has an executed result.
verification_levels.level: L4 software qualification on the host
verification_levels.purpose: Establish that the integrated software meets its software requirements on the host, as far as a host can show.
verification_levels.strategy: Run the requirement-level acceptance criteria against the host build. Every latency criterion in the three software requirements is a wall-clock criterion, and the host harness has no wall-clock oracle, so this level can only address the value criteria and not the timing ones.

verification_levels.blocker: No target-hardware execution exists anywhere in this corpus. This is not a resourcing gap that a plan can close; it requires hardware, a harness, and an authority to declare the product verified, none of which this corpus has.
verification_levels.level: L5 software qualification on target hardware
verification_levels.purpose: Establish that the software meets its requirements on the product's own hardware, under the real scheduler, the real peripherals and a real time base.
verification_levels.strategy: Not specified. There is nothing to specify against: no target board is described in this corpus, no harness for it exists, and no run has been performed.

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Transcribe a completed signature into the record as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block plus a revision_history entry naming the reviewer and citing this packet, and archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract.

target.primary_key_rule: ID-RULE-004-A1: an artefact identifier is unique within its profile; two records of different profiles may carry the same identifier string.
